But the specific name, attack capability, and targets are not known. It is too early to start guessing what the weapon is meant to attack.

The next shelf holds “counterspace.” In the U.S. Space Force’s framework, this term covers attacks and defenses carried out in orbit, through communication links, and on the ground. In other words, it is not the name of a single weapon in orbit.

The shelf of defenses holds a different range of items. These include warning of threats, making satellites tougher, splitting up their functions, spreading them out, making them able to move, and keeping backups. The U.S. Space Force also lists these steps as ways to protect satellites. They cannot be treated as the same thing as deploying an attack weapon in orbit.
